1 On Thursday the members oi the Liverpool and Din- -1 trig Grocers and Provision Dealers' Association paid a GM to the Sunlight Soap:corks and to the Ship Canal i works at F.asthatn. The party embarked at ten o'clock i ,on the steamer Sunlight, MSOnging to Messrs. Lever i and proceeded at once to the firin'o works, I rhetreherliwy were met by the mombem of the firm. Under the guidance of these gentlemen, the party were shown through the whole of the works, where they wonderingly marked the marvellous method and cleanli- ness of the operations through which the raw material passes before it assumos the well-known aspoet of Sun- light Soap. The Smiling, scenting, cooling, cutting, and pressing were all explained : and Messrs. Lever also showed the working of the machines for case-making, printing, and cther purposes. From the works Onlinev proceeded in the Sunlight to Ellesmere Port, there land- ing and walking along the route of the Ship Canal to 1 }lngham. The work of the steam navvies and dredger., Ithe hinging operations, and the pm-ogress of the works were fully investigated by many of the party. Tea wan partaken of at Eastham, under tim chairmanship of 4 Mr. J. Trantom, president of the association. After ton, the chairman proposed the health of Mr. Lever (bend of the :Sunlight firm), Mr. J. Lowrie seconding, to which : compliment Mr. toter suitably replied. Mr. B. SPGrana- han, seconded by Mr. G. Smith, proposed a vote of th snks to the chairman, this concluding the proceedings. The homeward journey wax then undertaken in the steamer.

A CHILI/ IN A ROILING FURNACE. On Thu,"lay, an inqiiest was held before the Shrews- bury Dietnet Coroner, on the body of Henry Howard Yates, seven years of age, who fell into a furnace filled with boiling mangolds, intended for pigs. The top of the boiler was three feet above the ground. and the lad stated that he climbed up and slipped in. lie was able to crawl out, hut died soon after. A verdict of acciden- tal death was returned. GRAVE SITUATION IN CRETE. .

..... ...... Despatches from Crete state that a large number of persons have been arcented in the island for conspiracy. Two hundred have been apprehended in the Heraelinn district atone. among them being several priests. The MetwitcAitan has formally protested to Chakir Pasha I (Governordieneral). but without effect. Further des- patcher of a disquieting nature have been received in Athens from Crete. The Turkish troopn, it is reported, continue to maltreat Christians and great panic conse- quently exists, the majority of the population having taken to ffi,ffit. In official circles in Athens the situation in the island is regarded as alarming.

div.head: RUNCORN REVISION COURT.
div.p: RUNCORN REVISION COURT.

On Wednesday, Mr. Clement Elphinstone Lloyd, revising barrister, held • court at Runcorn. for the purpose of revising the lists of voters for the polling : districts of Runcorn, North and South. Halton, and Aston. Mr. W. Handley represented the Liberals, and Mr. C. J. Hughes the Conservatives.

In Runcorn North, th;;;;W:44 old lodger Ci4iMS. Of who five were objected to ; 1.6 new lodger claims; 20 ownership claims (15 objected Sal and 47 occupiers claims. There were also five claimants under the ner- vine franchise, and three women claimed votes for local government purposcs. In Runcorn South there were 14 old lodger claims ; six new lodger claims (one objected to), nine ownership claims (two objected to) and 13 occupiers claims. Two women claimed votes for local government purp(sew.

The Conservatives t;l7‘itli;:l-a-;nrt.e..;i south Rank, as nlortgagts, in possession of leasehold p/nperty.—Mr. Handley pointed out that it was a mortgage on an under: lease, and that the assigner of the whole estate had also claimed; and he contended that the Let would not! allow an under lease as well as a lessee to have a vote for the same property.—Mr. Hughes said the claimant had a mortgage for £BOO upon houses, and he argued that this was sufficient to give a qualification.—Mr. Handley said it was the land that gave the qualification, and the Rev:sing Barrister stabs' that as the lessee had chosen to be registered for the whole estate, it was out pot his power to grant a vote for an under lease.--This decision also affected a claims made by the Liberals for a vote for property erected on the Poor's Field in Runcorn Muth. There was no other incidents of interest.

As this concluded Mr. I.7l;:drr. labours in the North- wieh Division, Mr. Hughes propowd a vote of thanks to him for his unvarying courtesy, and Mr. Handley sup- ported the proposition. The Reeking Barrister suitably replied, and in conclusion complimented the Runcorn overseer (Mr. Sutton) on the adinirable order in which he had presented his unto.
